done: BASE: master 119dcc3, in worktree concordance-2-count on branch live-card-count. One step, count. Scope: src/concordance/corpus.py, src/concordance/ops.py, src/concordance/capabilities.py, src/concordance/web/api.py (only where the serve path warms the corpus) and a new tests/test_live_card_count.py; any other path the builder finds it needs is a finding back to the lead before it is touched. It ships after green CI by an ordinary sh tools/deploy.sh of exactly those files, which restarts both engines once; no data file is sent, nothing is minted, no seal is made.

MEASURE, by the builder before the fix and re-done by the step's checker on its own, with python -I -B in a scratch keeping (CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR in a temporary directory, the corpus cache off), never pytest in the shared checkout: at 119dcc3's src, build the default corpus from a small cards.jsonl and receipt_cards.jsonl; (a) corpus.add_to_default of a new public card: card_count() and the browse total before and after; (b) a child process appends one card line to receipt_cards.jsonl the way cas._mint_receipt_card's cold path does (index=False): card_count() and get_card of its id in the parent before and after; (c) a fresh corpus built from the same files: its card_count(). The lead predicts (a) the count and browse total unchanged, (b) the count unchanged and get_card None, (c) both cards counted. The numbers are recorded in a note; if the reading is refuted, the run stops and says what was found instead.

STEP COUNT, ADD_CARD COMPLETE: after Corpus.add_card of a public card whose id is new to the keeping (neither resident nor in the frozen index), the corpus equals a fresh load of the same files (the card's line appended to an extra card source) in: card_count(); _public_sorted, order included; every _cids_by_call bucket, order included; every _call_tree count; _n; and the posting list of each of the card's tokens, order included. _public_sorted and the buckets are kept by inserting at the place the load's sort gives (key (call, title) and then id, which is the order the load's stable sort leaves), never by re-sorting the whole list; _n by adding one, never by walking every card as add_card does now. A card whose id is already in the keeping changes no count and no order (idempotent, as now); a card that is not public changes no count (as at the load). A card on a frozen shelf (corpus.frozen_shelves()) added live is held resident, so its count, _public_sorted, buckets, _call_tree and _n equal a fresh load while its tokens sit in the posting lists rather than the frozen document frequencies until the next restart; the plan claims no posting or search equality for it. Concurrent add_card calls are serialized by one lock, so a request thread's warm mint and the follower never interleave.

STEP COUNT, THE SUBSTANCE SPLIT: when ops' memo is already computed, add_card of a new card updates it in place so that ops.substance_if_cached() equals ops.substance(default_corpus().cards) after the add, every field, without walking the cards; when the memo is not yet computed, nothing is done (the background warm computes it over the cards it finds). The docstring premise at ops.py:105-106 is corrected to say the memo follows add_card.

STEP COUNT, THE FOLLOWER, in corpus.py: it follows exactly three files, the append-only card logs among EXTRA_CARD_SOURCES, beside the main cards file as the load resolves them: receipt_cards.jsonl (cas.py:211, opened 'a'), verified_cards.jsonl (science_cards.py, opened 'a'), acquired_cards.jsonl (tools/shepherd_rounds.py:216, opened 'a'). The one known rewriter, tools/graft_shelf_spines.py:181 (write_text over verified_cards.jsonl), is a one-shot tool followed by a restart. (a) START: each file's offset starts at the last line boundary at or before its size taken before the load began, so a line written while the load ran is read again, and any id already in the keeping is skipped: such a line is counted exactly once, whether the load took it or not, with the corpus cache off or on. (b) EACH POLL reads only the bytes past the offset, takes complete lines only (up to the last newline), parses each as load_cards' _line does (a line that is not a JSON object with an id is skipped, as at the load), adds each new id through add_card, and moves the offset past the last newline taken. (c) REWRITTEN: a file that shrank, whose device or inode changed, or whose 4,096 bytes before the offset no longer hash as remembered, is not followed again in this process; a file that grew by more than 16 MiB in one poll likewise; each is left to the next restart, and while any file is so left, capabilities' cards entry carries a 'note' naming it and saying that its changes are counted at the next restart. When nothing is left, the cards entry has exactly the fields it has now; only its count moves. (d) A poll never builds the corpus: it does nothing until corpus.loaded() is true, and never runs in a cell. (e) It runs on one daemon thread every 30 seconds, started once per serving process by the serve path after the corpus warm, so in nh-engine and nh-mcp alike; no CLI or one-shot process starts it, and a second start is a no-op. A poll's failure is logged and never stops the thread or a request.

THE PINS, all in the new tests/test_live_card_count.py, each over a scratch keeping in a temporary directory, each red with the base's src (the pin check) and green with the step: (1) add_card equality with a fresh load, every structure item 3 names, over a keeping with at least two calls and two cards tied on (call, title); (2) a second add_card of the same id changes nothing; (3) cross-process: a child process running cas._mint_receipt_card with index=False (the mint's path) appends receipt cards; after one poll in the parent, card_count() and capabilities.statement()'s cards count are up by exactly that number, get_card finds each, and the corpus object is the same one (no rebuild); (4) a torn last line is not taken until its newline arrives, and then taken once; (5) a line appended during the load (through a hook the test installs between the size reading and the end of the load) is counted exactly once, with the corpus cache off and, if it can be turned on in a scratch keeping, on; (6) a rewritten file (os.replace with new content, and a truncation) is left alone: the count unchanged and the statement's cards entry carrying the note; with no file left, the entry's keys equal the base's; (7) after adds with the substance memo computed, substance_if_cached() equals substance(cards); (8) a poll with no corpus loaded builds none and adds nothing; (9) the follower starts once however often it is asked. The existing tests that touch these paths still pass unchanged: tests/test_receipt_is_also_a_card.py, tests/test_connect.py, tests/test_expand.py and every test file naming capabilities or substance. No existing assert is removed or loosened.

GATES: the builder gate on the step's paths; the checker's own full gate on the same content against docs/harness/baseline.txt; the moat FALSE-POSITIVES 0. A red whose only cause is a timeout is re-run once and both results are recorded in a note before any verdict relies on them; any other red stays red. CI must be green in both jobs on the branch push and on master before the deploy, with the gate's passed count up by the new tests' count and skipped unchanged against 119dcc3's master run, any other change named.

LIVE: a checker takes the live-before snapshot before the push (rule live-before-and-after) on narrowhighway.com, narrowhighway.org and api.narrowhighway.com: /health, /capabilities without its cache block, every /seals hash with its page's sha256, /ledger/verify, public GETs only, plus one read-only MCP tools/call of capabilities on the MCP host, the one POST this plan names. The lead deploys exactly the step's files and records in the ship note the deploy's gates, the engines' MainPID and NRestarts before and after, and the box copy of each shipped file read through tools/verify_deploy.py's own functions as in run 2026-11-14-power-floor-pipe (no EXTRA name, no ssh error text quoted). LIVE-AFTER: every field identical except /health's restart counters and each surface's cards count, which may differ from the before only by cards added since, named (new seals as traffic, /seals' receipt_cards growth); no 'note' in any cards entry. THE MOVE WITHOUT A RESTART: nothing in this run writes to the keeping, so it is graded at the first new receipt card after the deploy: the checker reads every surface's cards count and /seals' receipt_cards at two times, the lead's note showing both engines' MainPID unchanged between them; where receipt_cards grew by k, every surface's count must have grown by at least k, the MCP host's included. If no new receipt card arrives in the live window, the live verdict says the move is not yet seen on the box, and the run records it as pending, to be graded at the next mint, never as seen.

REVERT, named: the deploy's rollback directory holds the snapshot of the shipped files, and git revert of the step's commit restores the base; nothing in the keeping depends on the step, since it writes nothing.
goal: Make the keeping's card count follow the keeping while the engine runs, asked by the owner 2026-11-15 ('it should be set to update automatically'), after checker-108 saw /capabilities' card count rise by 9 only at the deploy's restart, nine cards the sky mint had written (run 2026-11-14-power-floor-pipe line 25). THE GAP, as the lead reads it at 119dcc3, in three parts. (1) capabilities._substrate reports corpus.card_count(), which is len(_public_sorted), built once at the load (src/concordance/corpus.py:502). Corpus.add_card (corpus.py:698), the live path every in-process addition takes through corpus.add_to_default (cas._mint_receipt_card's warm path, science_cards, find, expand, tools/shepherd_rounds.py), puts the card into cards, _by_token and _cids_by_call but never into _public_sorted or _call_tree, so even a seal made inside the engine moves neither the count, the browse totals (corpus.py:606 and 614) nor stats() until a restart. (2) A mint runs in its own process (tools/stick_mint.py, the cold path, index=False) and appends to data/receipt_cards.jsonl and data/verified_cards.jsonl, which a running engine reads only at its load (EXTRA_CARD_SOURCES, corpus.py:1093), so its cards join only at the next restart; the same holds between the two serving processes, nh-engine and nh-mcp (both run python -m concordance serve, deploy/nh-engine.service:19 and deploy/nh-mcp.service:19): a seal made through one appends a receipt card the other never reads until it restarts. (3) ops.substance_of_the_keeping memoizes the substance split on the premise 'The corpus is immutable under a running service' (src/concordance/ops.py:105-106), which add_card already breaks. THE FIX: add_card leaves the corpus as a fresh load of the same files would hold it, the memoized substance split is kept equal to a recount, and each serving process follows the three append-only card logs, adding each new card through add_card, so a card written by any process is counted within one poll, without a restart. Nothing is removed from a live keeping; a file that is rewritten instead of appended is left to the next restart and said so in the capability statement.

checker-109, MEASURE (plan item 2), done on its own at 119dcc3's src: python -I -B, CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR a fresh temporary directory, CONCORDANCE_CORPUS_CACHE=0, no freeze set, no pytest, nothing in either checkout touched. Keeping: cards.jsonl with 6 lines (5 public, two of them on one call and tied on (call, title), the higher id written first; 1 public_review), receipt_cards.jsonl with the receipt spine and one receipt card. At the load: card_count() 7; _public_sorted equals the ids sorted by (call, title, id), the tie broken by id; every _cids_by_call bucket is sorted by id.
(a) corpus.add_to_default of a new public card c_new (same shelf and title as c_a, so the same call): card_count() 7 to 7, browse()['total'] 7 to 7, call_total('') 7 to 7, stats()['total'] 7 to 7, _n 7 to 8. c_new is not in _public_sorted; get_card finds it; its bucket is [c_a, c_new], appended; the posting lists are no longer all sorted; ops.substance_if_cached()['total'] stays 8 while ops.substance(cards) recounts 9. A second add_to_default of c_new left _public_sorted, the buckets, _call_tree, _n and the postings identical. Re-adding the resident public_review card with lifecycle_stage public (the path find._set_stage takes): get_card finds it, card_count() 7 to 7.
(b) a child python -I -B ran cas._mint_receipt_card(h, record, index=False): exit 0, and it appended 2 lines, card_spine_seals again and then card_seal_9a485baa7a5a...; in the parent card_count() 7 to 7, and get_card of the new id None before and after.
(c) corpus._DEFAULT reset and a fresh corpus built from the same files: card_count() 8, get_card finds the child's card. The 8 is the 7 plus the child's receipt card: the second spine line is the same id and counts once, and c_new was never written to any file, so no fresh load can hold it. So (a) and (b) are as the lead predicted; (c) counts the child's card, not 'both', because the in-process add writes no file. The reading of the gap stands.
Also measured, for the plan review: one call holding titles 'Tied' (id c_1) and 'tied' (id c_0) gives the bucket [c_0, c_1] and _public_sorted [c_1, c_0]. And with a Corpus of 60,000 resident cards, 300 add_card calls on a second thread 10 ms apart while a reader thread looped: RuntimeError 'dictionary changed size during iteration' in 189 of 386 loops over cards.values(), 65 of 386 ops.substance(cards), 11 of 386 cids_for_call, and 0 of 386 over _by_token.items(). Scripts and their output are in the checker's scratch folder.

findings: GOAL and item 5, the reading of the writers misses a fourth runtime card log and a second rewriter. (i) web_cache.jsonl is in EXTRA_CARD_SOURCES (corpus.py:1207), and both serving processes append to it at runtime and then call add_to_default: expand.py:370-391 (the /search slow lane and the /ask acquisition) and find.py:586-614 (the tortoise). find._set_stage (find.py:470-505) also rewrites it whole with a tmp file and os.replace, then re-adds the card, when a steward promotes or refuses an acquisition (shelves.py:784-786) and when a human ask releases a held one (find.py:628). So a card that nh-engine acquires is never counted by nh-mcp until a restart, and the reverse, and the goal's 'a card written by any process is counted within one poll' is false for these cards. (ii) tools/classify_keeping.py --apply rewrites every *_cards.jsonl (card_files, :87), the three followed files included, by tmp plus os.replace (:119-137), so tools/graft_shelf_spines.py:181 is not 'the one known rewriter'. The inode test catches os.replace, so only the reading is wrong here. NEEDED: name web_cache.jsonl, and either follow it (and say that its first rewrite ends following it in that process, with the note) or leave it alone by name in the goal and in the capability statement. If it is left alone, LIVE-AFTER must allow nh-engine's count and the MCP host's count to differ by each engine's own acquisitions. Also name classify_keeping --apply as a rewriter of all three files.

Item 3, an id already in the keeping: '(idempotent, as now)' does not describe 119dcc3. Today a re-add replaces the dict (corpus.py:705), and find._set_stage depends on that to release a held card (find.py:474-475 and 499-504: 'refreshes the live corpus so the change is visible on this request'). It re-adds a resident public_review id as public. Measured: get_card then finds the card, and card_count() stays 7, while a fresh load of the rewritten file counts it. Under the plan's words a builder can (a) return early, which breaks the release live (get_card stays None until a restart, and no test reads the live corpus after curate; tests/test_expand_on_call.py:260-266 reads only the file), or (b) replace the dict but 'change no count', which leaves the corpus unequal to a fresh load. NEEDED: state the rule for an id that is already resident. Its dict is replaced as now. If it is now public and was not, it enters card_count, _public_sorted, its bucket, _call_tree, _n and its postings at the load's places. If its publicness is unchanged, no count or order moves. A public card turning non-public has no in-tree caller: leave it alone by name. An id in the frozen index is skipped. Add a pin: on a loaded corpus, find._promote_to_public of a held card, then get_card finds it and the corpus equals a fresh load.

Item 3 and pin (1), the orders: the plan says the buckets are kept by '(call, title) and then id', but the load sorts each bucket by id alone (corpus.py:500-501), and one call can hold two different titles. Measured: titles 'Tied' (id c_1) and 'tied' (id c_0) share the call alpha.t.ti.tied, the bucket is [c_0, c_1], and _public_sorted is [c_1, c_0]. Pin (1)'s keeping ('two calls and two cards tied on (call, title)') does not exercise this, and it also lets an append pass wherever the new card happens to sort last. Also, '_n by adding one' is not a fresh load when no public card was held, since _n = max(1, ...) (corpus.py:467). NEEDED: buckets are kept in id order and _public_sorted in (call, title, id) order. The keeping of pin (1) must hold a new card whose place is strictly inside _public_sorted, inside its bucket and inside at least one posting list. It must also hold a (call, title) tie that the new id breaks by sorting first, and one call with two titles whose id order is not their title order. Keep _n equal to max(1, public count). Either pin the frozen-shelf equality the item claims (frozen_shelves can be monkeypatched for the load), or drop that claim.

Items 3, 4 and 5(e), readers on other threads: 'one lock' serializes writers only. Request threads loop over the very dicts that add_card grows in place: decks.py:377, floor.py:86, codex.py:201 and 279, ask.py:667, the sitemap at web/api.py:593 (its except turns the error into a sitemap with no card in it), cids_for_call at corpus.py:623 (browse by call), corpus.py:2260 and 2282. The substance walk at ops.py:61 runs in the nh-warm-substance thread (web/api.py:4304-4311). Measured at 119dcc3: with 60,000 resident cards and 300 add_card calls on a second thread 10 ms apart, 'dictionary changed size during iteration' was raised in 189 of 386 loops over cards.values(), in 65 of 386 ops.substance(cards) calls and in 11 of 386 cids_for_call calls. Today only a warm mint adds. The follower turns every card from the other process into an add on a background thread, in both engines, and its first poll at boot lands while the substance walk runs. An error there is swallowed, so the split is never served until the next restart; an add that lands after the walk and before the memo is set is lost from the memo for good (item 4 says 'nothing is done'). 5(e)'s 'never stops ... a request' is therefore not met. NEEDED: say how a reader stays safe within corpus.py and ops.py, for example copy-on-write of the dicts add_card grows (one copy per poll, its memory measured at the box's sizes), and the substance walk and the memo update ordered under the add lock. Add a deterministic pin with no sleep: take an iterator over cards.values() and one over _cids_by_call.items(), call next() once, add_card a new card, and finish both with no RuntimeError. Add a second pin where an add during a patched substance walk still leaves substance_if_cached() equal to substance(cards).

Item 5(a) and pin (5), the corpus-cache hit: CONCORDANCE_CORPUS_CACHE is on by default (corpus_cache.py:64-75). On a hit, default_corpus returns Corpus._restore (corpus.py:1702-1721), which runs neither __init__ nor load_cards. Two results. (i) The sizes must be read before the cache key is made (corpus.py:1697), not where load_cards starts. (ii) Any state the step adds to the instance (the add lock, the follower's state) must also be set in _restore (corpus.py:521-529). Otherwise every add on a restored corpus raises, and every caller swallows it (cas.py:227-228, science_cards.py:150-151, expand.py:392, find.py:503 and 613): the count never moves and nothing says why. With the default on, tools/deploy.sh restarts nh-mcp (:151-154) just after nh-engine has saved that cache, so nh-mcp is likely to run a restored corpus right after this ship. Pin (5)'s 'if it can be turned on' is soft: it can be, and CONCORDANCE_CORPUS_CACHE_DIR relocates it. NEEDED: pin (5) as three deterministic cases, built by monkeypatching corpus.load_cards and corpus_cache.load with no thread and no sleep. A line appended before load_cards reads the file is taken by the load and skipped by the poll. A line appended after it is taken by the poll. On a hit asserted as LOAD_PHASES['corpus_cache'] == 'hit', a line appended after the key is made is taken by the poll. Each counts once. Pins (1) and (3) also run on a corpus restored from the cache.

Item 6, the pins against the base, and the thread they leave: (2) 'a second add_card of the same id changes nothing' is green at the base. Measured at 119dcc3: after a second add, _public_sorted, the buckets, _call_tree, _n and the postings were identical. That contradicts 'each red with the base's src'. (8) and (9) are red at the base only because the poll and start functions do not exist. Separately, (9) has to start the follower, which polls every 30 s and never stops (5(e)). Inside the shared pytest process it would keep reading whatever CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR a later test sets and adding cards to that test's corpus. NEEDED: state (2) as 'after a second add the corpus still equals a fresh load', which is red at the base, or say which pins are red only by absence. Give the follower a stop that a test can set, or check once-ness without a live polling loop, so that no follower thread outlives its test.

Goal and item 5(c), the rewrite test's limits and a late file: the goal says 'a file that is rewritten instead of appended is left to the next restart and said so in the capability statement'. The three tests miss an in-place rewrite (write_text keeps the inode, graft_shelf_spines.py:181) that keeps the size or grows while leaving the 4,096 bytes before the offset unchanged. No note is shown for such a rewrite. A same-size rewrite is not seen. The plan also does not say what happens to a followed file that is absent when the process starts and appears later. A fresh load reads it, but a follower with no starting offset can miss it until a restart. NEEDED: state the limit in the goal and in item 5(c), or add a test that closes it, for example an mtime change with no growth counted as a rewrite. Say that a file absent at the start is followed from offset 0 once it appears, with its device and inode taken then.

Item 8, LIVE: (i) /seals' receipt_cards counts non-empty lines, not cards (seals.py:33-38 and 81). The cold path writes the spine again in each mint process: measured, one child mint appended 2 lines for 1 new card, and the sky mint added 10 lines for 9 cards. cas.store's heal (cas.py:78-81) also writes a receipt again in an engine that does not hold it yet. So 'where receipt_cards grew by k, every surface's count must have grown by at least k' fails a correct follower at a mint like the one that started this run. NEEDED: grade by distinct new ids. Use each new seal hash on /seals whose GET /card?id=card_seal_<hash> answers 200 on narrowhighway.com and narrowhighway.org with MainPID unchanged, plus the MCP host's count. Or read the appended lines with GET /sync/file?name=receipt_cards.jsonl and a Range header (an allow-listed *_cards.jsonl, web/api.py:3425), and name whichever is used. (ii) LIVE-AFTER lets only cards.count differ. But cards_substance.count, cards_stubs (its count and the stub_ratio in its means) and cards_frozen move with the same cards: checker-108's diff at power-floor-pipe line 25 shows substance +9 and stub_ratio 0.04 to 0.0399. The restart also adds every card written since the old engines booted, warm seals included, since at the base add_card never moves the count. 'Added since' the snapshot does not cover those; the reference is receipt_cards 2471 at power-floor-pipe line 25. (iii) Name the MCP URL: https://api.narrowhighway.com/mcp reaches nh-mcp (deploy/Caddyfile:19-20), while narrowhighway.com/mcp reaches nh-engine. Say that the one POST is made once per reading: before, after, and the two move readings. (iv) Once the run is recorded, a 'pending' move has no owner. Name where and by whom it is graded, for example a want carried into the next mint run's live-after, or hold the live verdict until it is seen.

Item 1, smallest: the one step bundles two independently useful changes. The first is add_card complete plus the substance memo: with only that, a seal or acquisition made inside an engine moves that engine's own count. The second is the follower, its capability note and its start in the serve path, which needs the first. docs/HARNESS.md, 'What smallest and faithful mean', says: 'If it could be split into two independently useful steps, it is two steps.' The follower is also where the thread, file and restart risks sit. NEEDED: two steps, count-add-card (items 3 and 4, pins 1, 2 and 7) and then count-follower (item 5, pins 3 to 6, 8 and 9), each with its own pin check. Otherwise, the plan says why one step is the smallest.

Goal and item 3, what still reads the keeping as it was at the load, and one visible consequence: corpus.daily (corpus.py:2222) picks the card of the day as hash % len(_public_sorted). With the count moving, the card of the day changes at every add during the day; today it changes only at a restart. It is served at /daily, by MCP daily_card and by lighthouse_node. The plan does not name this. It also names nothing that stays as at the load: graph._GRAPH and its memoized overview (graph.py:101-107 and 129, per-shelf counts); ask._discern_watch (ask.py:655-674); the bridge overlays (a row that names a live-added id stays unresolved, corpus.py:1426-1437); _dedupe_connections, which runs at the load's gate (corpus.py:1340) and not in add_card; _frozen_shelf_counts; the order of the cards dict; call_children's order among equal counts (corpus.py:606 and 610); and, for a card on a frozen shelf, get_card (live it is the whole card; a fresh load gives the shard's copy or a stub) and the substance split (counted live, dropped at the next restart). NEEDED: either accept the daily card's moving by name or keep the day's pick stable, and say that each of the others is left alone until a restart (or include it), so that 'equals a fresh load' is read only for the structures item 3 lists.

(1) COPY-ON-WRITE AT THE BOX'S SIZES (83,488 resident cards, 840,886 frozen-index ids, 924,279 public ids): copy of the cards dict 3.7 ms. Copy of _public_sorted, a list of 924,279 ids: 49 to 51 ms with the ids in shuffled allocation order, 50.0 ms with interned ids, 25.7 ms with ids allocated in sorted order; a bisect insert into the same list in place 0.02 ms. One posting list of 80,000 ids: copy 2.31 ms, in-place insort 0.66 ms. Copy and insert of 50 such lists 199 ms (tracemalloc peak 34.3 MiB), of 150 such 598 ms (103.0 MiB). The tokenizer keeps every word of two letters or more (corpus.py:46-47), so a common word's posting list holds most of the 83,393 resident public cards.
(2) TIMESTAMPS: an in-place, same-size rewrite of an early line, made right after an append and a stat, left (size, mtime_ns) unchanged in 34 of 200 trials, in a temporary directory on this Windows laptop (NTFS).
(3) sha256 of 5,918,349 bytes read from disk: 9.4 ms.
(4) PUBLIC GETs, a generic client, no redirect followed. 13:17:40 UTC, GET https://narrowhighway.com/seals: 200, 999 bytes, its seals object holding exactly broken_links, cas_bad, cas_records, cite_url, minted, newest, ok, oldest, re_verified_at, receipt_cards, tampered, total_checksum, verified and verified_of, and no seal hash: minted 1823, receipt_cards 2473, cas_records 3191, newest 2026-11-14T16:46:56 (at line 25 of run 2026-11-14-power-floor-pipe: 1823, 2471 and 3189). 13:17:51 to 13:18:04 UTC, four GETs of https://narrowhighway.com/sync/file?name=receipt_cards.jsonl with Range bytes=33554432-, bytes=8388608-, bytes=4194304- and bytes=2097152-, each body cut off by curl's size cap: 416, 416, then 206 with Content-Range bytes 4194304-5918348/5918349 and 206 with bytes 2097152-5918348/5918349, the same X-Sha256 79d82f5df1d3.. both times. findings: Item 5 (READERS STAY SAFE) and item 2(d): copying every changed list on each add costs about item 2(d)'s whole budget, and it runs on a request thread. Measured (line 6): a copy of _public_sorted at 924,279 ids takes 25 to 51 ms, and a copy of one 80,000-id posting list 2.3 ms. The tokenizer keeps stopwords (corpus.py:46-47), so each common word of a card copies a list that holds most resident public cards; 50 such lists took 199 ms. A list copy runs in C under the GIL, so every add stalls every request thread of that engine for that long. A warm seal makes two or three adds on its own request thread: the receipt and the spine (cas.py:220-222) and the verified card (science_cards.py:146-149). Item 2(d)'s stop rule (50 ms for a batch of 10) will likely stop step one. A synthetic corpus with short posting lists, or with ids allocated in sorted order, would pass that rule while the box pays more. Only dicts raise when they change during iteration; a list changed in place under the add lock raises nothing (in place, measured: 0.02 ms for _public_sorted, 0.66 ms for an 80,000-id list). NEEDED: decide the list design now. Either copy only the dicts (the cards dict, 3.7 ms; _cids_by_call, a _call_tree level and _by_token only when a key is new) and insert into lists in place under the add lock, naming what a concurrent list reader may see (one id yielded twice or skipped once, in stats(), health() or a search's candidate walk) and giving the card of the day its own copy of the public ids, taken at the load or restore. Item 8(c) and count-follower pin (4): re-hashing only when the size or mtime changed misses an in-place, same-size rewrite made in the same timestamp tick as the last append. Measured (line 6): 34 of 200 such rewrites left (size, mtime_ns) unchanged on Windows NTFS. Linux also takes inode timestamps from a coarse clock (one tick) unless the kernel has multigrain timestamps (6.13 and later). So pin (4)'s 'in-place same-size change of an early line', made milliseconds after the poll, goes red at random, in CI's windows job at least, and 8(c)'s 'sees any rewrite of bytes it has read' is not true for that case. The plan also does not say when [0, offset) is first hashed. If it is hashed at the follower's start, after the warm, a rewrite made during the load becomes the baseline and is never seen. NEEDED: hash [0, offset) on every poll (measured: 9.4 ms for 5,918,349 bytes, the box's receipt_cards.jsonl size read at line 6; hashlib releases the GIL for large buffers). Or keep the mtime gate, state the same-tick limit, and make pin (4) set a distinct mtime with os.utime(ns=...). Also take the first hash at the size reading, before the load, or state the boot-window limit.

Item 9, LIVE: /seals lists no seal hash, so neither 'each /seals hash absent from line 25's reading' nor 'every seal hash new on /seals' can be read. seals.summary (seals.py:51-92) serves counts, a root checksum and dates. (My finding at line 4 proposed reading hashes from /seals. That was wrong.) NEEDED: name the read. GET https://narrowhighway.com/sync/file?name=receipt_cards.jsonl is allow-listed (replicate.py:48, '*_cards.jsonl'), and a Range request answers 206 with the file's total (line 6: bytes 4194304-5918348/5918349). The first reading takes the whole file once. The AFTER's named cards are the distinct ids in lines past 2471 that are not in lines 1 to 2471. Each later reading asks for Range bytes=<previous total>-. verified_cards.jsonl and acquired_cards.jsonl can be read the same way to name more of the remainder. web_cache.jsonl is on replicate's NEVER list (replicate.py:55), so its share stays named but unread. THE MOVE: read the counts at least two polls (60 s) after the file reading that names the ids, because a line appended in the last 30 s may not have been polled yet. The bar is the number of distinct receipt ids new to the file in the window. Also say that /card answering on nh-engine proves nothing for a card nh-engine minted itself, since its own warm add answers /card at 119dcc3 too; for those cards the MCP host's count is the follower's test.

A new id joins a copy of the cards dict, one copy per batch, swapped in under the lock. A public new id is placed by bisect insert: into _public_sorted by (call, title, id), and into its bucket and each token's posting list by id. Every _call_tree count moves through _count_call, and _n comes from the kept count, with no walk. A resident id's dict is replaced in place. A withheld card turned public enters every structure; when publicness is unchanged, nothing moves. _withheld_listed keeps a public card turned withheld from being listed twice. Only the cards dict and the _call_tree levels are copied and swapped. _by_token and _cids_by_call grow in place. Each of the five loops over them outside __init__ (footprint's two, _index_card_ids, gauges, cids_for_call) runs through _walk_whole, which restarts only on a RuntimeError of exactly that type and message, at most three times, and then walks a list(d) key snapshot. The build holds built._add_lock from _DEFAULT = built through the cache save and prune. _restore sets _add_lock, _n_public, _withheld_listed and _daily_ids. daily picks over _daily_ids. Every add to _DEFAULT calls ops.substance_note inside the lock, and the walk takes its snapshot and settles under the lock. There is no lock-order cycle: the walk takes _SUBSTANCE_WALK and then the add lock, and add_cards takes no other lock. No existing test or assert changed; the only tests/ changes are the new file and one manifest line.
NOT HELD, measured with my own scripts:
(1) THE DISPLACED KEY (the build note's second named difference). The keeping is 15 public cards titled B00, B02 ... B28 on shelf alpha. c_b14 sits at index 7 of _public_sorted, the first place bisect probes. It is re-added, still public, with title Z99, so its call and title change and it keeps its old place (item 3(iii), left alone). Then B25 and B21 are added as new cards. Live _public_sorted by title: B00 B02 B04 B06 B08 B10 B12 B21 B25 Z99 B16 B18 B20 B22 B24 B26 B28. A fresh load of the same files with the three lines appended: B00 B02 B04 B06 B08 B10 B12 B16 B18 B20 B21 B22 B24 B25 B26 B28 Z99. With c_b14 taken out of both lists they still differ: B25 is 8th among the others live and 13th in the fresh load; B21 is 7th and 10th. The cause: insort compares each probe by _sort_key, which reads the replaced dict's new (call, title) while the id still sits at its old place, so the list is no longer sorted under the key bisect relies on. Every later insert whose search reaches that id can land out of order, and each card that lands out of order misleads the inserts after it, until a restart. A public card turned withheld (_withheld_listed) whose title changed does the same. Items 3(iii) and 4 leave alone only that one card's own place and postings; nothing names the other cards' places, and item 3(ii) puts each new public card at its (call, title, id) place. So this is a defect, not something the left-alone list covers. It reaches the box only when a listed public card is re-added under a different call or title. No step-one caller does that in the ordinary course; step two's follower will, whenever a followed file gains a line for a resident id under another title.
(2) PIN (4)'s FOOTPRINT CASE lands its adds only in footprint's first walk over _by_token, the postings sum. With _walk_whole spied, footprint() made two calls: ('values', 12 keys before, 16 after) and ('items', 16, 16). The hook counts only len() and iter(), and the second walk reads each list through sys.getsizeof. HELD, ITEM 8.
(a) follow_start(path) runs in default_corpus right after its timers start, before the corpus cache key is made and before load_cards. Its result is set on the restored corpus (restored._follow) and on the built one (built._follow) before either becomes _DEFAULT. The start reading reads each file in 1 MiB chunks; the offset is the last newline read, and the sha256 is of exactly [0, offset). An absent file starts at 0 (seen False).
(b) poll_followed takes complete lines only (up to the last newline) and parses them as load_cards' _line does: strip, json.loads, the same two errors skipped, a dict with an id kept. The poll's cards from all files go into ONE add_cards batch. Each offset moves, and its hash takes exactly the bytes taken, only after add_cards returns.
(c) _follow_read opens ONE descriptor, re-hashes [0, offset) on every poll whatever the size or mtime, then reads at most 16 MiB + 1 past it from the same descriptor. A file that is shorter, gone once seen, hashes differently or grew past 16 MiB is left: logged, never read again in this process, and swapped into a new 'left' dict. capabilities' cards entry gains 'note' only while a file is left; otherwise its keys are exactly count and means (pinned before and after).
(d) poll_followed returns 0 in a cell and reads _DEFAULT directly, never default_corpus.
(e) start_follower makes one daemon thread, nh-follow-cards, with a 30 s Event wait. A second start while it runs returns False. stop_follower sets the Event and joins, so the thread ends at its next wake. A poll's exception is logged and the loop goes on. Only build_server's warm branch calls it. nh-engine (serve_many: only its first listener warms) and nh-mcp (serve) both run that path, per deploy/*.service. Every build_server call in tests passes warm=False, and nothing else calls start_follower. The pins' fixture asserts stop_follower(timeout=10) after each test, so no test leaves a follower alive.
FOLLOWED: exactly receipt_cards.jsonl, acquired_cards.jsonl and verified_cards.jsonl beside _cards_path(), in the load's order. web_cache.jsonl and every other source are not in FOLLOWED_CARD_SOURCES, and pin (8) shows a web_cache line is not taken.
ITEM 9: the 16 ids pin the eight behaviours as written, each red at ef62b7c by absence (my gate: 16 red). Suite 5853 passed and 236 skipped: up by exactly 16 against step one's 5837, skipped unchanged.
JUDGED, the points the build note names beside the plan, none a finding:
(1) An explicit cards path follows nothing: right, since load_cards(path) reads no extra source, and the serve path builds with no path.
(2) A file unreadable at the start is left with the note: the conservative reading. A load that cannot read it would fail anyway.
(3) 'Gone' applies only once a file has been seen: consistent with (5), a file absent at the start being waited for.
(4) The batch takes files in the load's order: so a later file's line for an id wins, as at a load.
(5) A failed add_cards moves no offset, so the next poll retries. A line that makes add_cards raise (a non-string id, title or call) would also fail the boot's own load, so the follower is no less robust than the load. A failure partway through add_cards could leave a card resident but unlisted until a restart; that is step one's exception safety, reached only by such a line.
(6) The grew_past_the_cap case (the cap monkeypatched to 64 bytes) is a fair stand-in for 16 MiB.
(7) THE RE-READ AND BRIDGE EDGES, measured by my own probe (m_bridge.py). A reference_bridges.jsonl row c_a -cites-> card_spine_seals; at the load the spine carries part_of the Floor and c_a cited_by. A child's cold mint writes the spine again and one receipt. After one poll (2 cards taken, the count up by 1), the spine carries only part_of the Floor while c_a keeps its cites edge; a fresh load has both. So the live graph loses the overlay's reverse edge on that card until a restart. This is WITHIN the plan: item 3 defines each added card's dict as equal to a fresh load's 'less any edge a bridge overlay row would attach', and the re-read card passes through add_cards; its dict is exactly that. Nothing else the load puts on a dict is lost on a re-read. shelve's call and facets and _dedupe_connections are applied again by add_cards. __init__'s call is shelve's. A frozen id is skipped, never re-read. graft_shelf_spines writes its member_of edges into the file lines themselves, and its in-place rewrite of verified_cards.jsonl leaves that file to the restart. cas writes its part_of link in the line. graph.py builds its own structures and changes no card dict. On the box: no tracked overlay names a receipt, verified or acquired card or the spine (grep of the five tracked overlays). The two box-owned overlays come from compendium (works_bridges: endpoints are cards with a source.domain, which the receipt cards and the spine lack) and from the seed tools (chain_bridges: chain node ids). So it reaches nothing there today. If an overlay ever names a followed card, carrying the overlay's edges over on a re-read would be a want, not this step's.
(8) The Windows os.replace window, checked on this laptop: os.replace onto a file another handle holds open raises PermissionError (winerror 5), and succeeds once it is closed. A poll holds each followed file about 10 ms every 30 s, so on Windows a one-shot tool's os.replace onto a followed file (classify_keeping --apply) can fail in that window and leave the old file whole. The box is Linux, where it cannot.
